pressReleaseTitle: India Ratings Affirms B.G. Shirke Construction Technology at ‘IND A’/ Stable; Rates Additional Loans
issuerName: B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt. Ltd.
overview: India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) has affirmed B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt. Ltd’s (BGSCTPL) Long-Term Issuer Rating at ‘IND A’. The Outlook is Stable. The instrument-wise rating actions are as follows:
keyRatingDrivers:
Strong Revenue Traction and Visibility: BGSCTPL recorded a steady increase in revenue over FY18-FY19, supported by higher order inflows and strong execution of its order book. The company’s revenues increased by 17% yoy to INR33.9 billion in FY19 (FY18: growth of 12% yoy to INR28.9 billion).

 

Ind-Ra expects BGSCTPL to report strong revenue growth of more than 10% each in FY20 and FY21 on the back of strong order position of INR177 billion (5.2x of FY19 revenue) as of October 2019  (INR140.6 billion as of August 2018; 4.5x of FY18 revenue) and its strong execution capabilities. Revenue from construction contracts accounted for about 94% of the revenue in 1HFY20 (FY19:94% and FY18: 93%).

 

The company’s EBITDA margin remained almost flat at 20% in 1HFY20 (FY19: 19.5% and FY18: 19.4%). BGSCTPL has a price escalation clause for majority of its contracts, thus protecting its margins from fluctuation in cost of key raw material such as steel and cement, which account for around 30%-35% of the company’s total operating cost.

 

The margins remained high in FY19 due to high-margin projects from CIDCO and MHADA (FY18: included one-time escalation from erstwhile projects). Excluding the one-time rebate/ claims, the EBITDA margin for FY18 stood at 16.5%. The company booked revenues of INR19.2 billion in 1HFY20, with an EBITDA margin of 20%.

 

Ind-Ra expects BGSCTPL’s EBITDA margins to remain in the range of 19%-20% in FY20, supported by one-off of INR1.6 billion in FY20 pertaining to old projects.

 

Robust-but-Concentrated Order Book; Adequate Competitive Position: At end-October 2019, BGSCTPL had an unexecuted order book of INR177.4 billion (end-August 2018: INR140.6 billion; end-June 2017: INR149 billion), which translates into 5.2x of FY19 revenues (FY18: 4.5x; FY17: 5.9x). Customer concentration remained high as of end-October 2019, with Delhi Development Authority (DDA) representing 25% (end of August 2018: 45%), Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA) accounting for 15% (21%), City and Industrial Development Corporation (CIDCO) constituting 40% (majority received between April-October 2019; 13%) and MHADA-Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) accounting for 10% (12%) of the order book. Moreover, the share of the top 10 projects in the order book increased to 69% at end-October (end-August 2018: 60.6%).

 

Slow-moving/stalled projects (typically classified as projects awarded over FY09-FY15), largely consisting of orders bagged from MHADA, accounted for 6% of the order book at end of October 2019 (end of August for orders awarded over FY09-FY14: 11%).

 

Delay in commencement of large housing projects awarded by DDA in FY16 was owing to deferred approvals, which were finally received in June 2017. At end-October 2019, work was yet to commence on about 40% of the total orders. Majority of these orders were received between April-October 2019 (mainly from CIDCO; FY19: 16%; FY18: 14%). As confirmed by the management, the company has received approvals for majority of its order book for commencement of construction. Thus, no delay in project execution is likely in the near-to-medium term.

 

BGSCTPL continues to have a strong competitive position in the prefabricated housing industry, with an established operating record of over 30 years. The strong competitive position benefits the company in terms of meeting prequalification criteria when bidding for new projects of similar types.

 

Continued Strong Credit Metrics: BGSCTPL's on-balance sheet debt rose by 16.8% to INR11.9 billion as the company took an additional term loan to fund the purchase of additional machinery to set up factories at CIDCO. The net leverage (net on-balance sheet debt/ operating EBITDAR) improved to 1.25x in FY19 (FY18: 1.4x), primarily driven by a rise in EBITDA. The gross interest coverage (operating EBITDAR/gross interest expense) remained stable at 3.37x in FY19 (FY18: 3.32x), as the rise in EBITDA was marginally higher than that in interest expenses.

 

At FYE19, BGSCTPL had given a corporate guarantee of INR0.3 billion (FY18: INR0.4 billion) to B. G. Shirke Oil & Gas India Private Limited, and a letter of undertaking for INR0.8 billion (FY18: Nil) to the lender of Teenmurty Summit Realty LLP. The adjusted gross debt rose by 23% yoy to INR12.3 billion in FY19, and consequently, net adjusted leverage (adjusted net debt/operating EBITDAR) improved marginally to 1.41x (FY18: 1.46x). Ind-Ra expects BGSCTPL’s credit metrics to sustain at the same levels in the near term and gradually improve in the medium term on account of healthy medium-term revenue visibility and limited increase in debt.

 

Liquidity Indicator - Adequate: BGSCTPL had cash and cash equivalents of INR2.4 million at FYE19 (FYE18: INR1.3 billion). Despite the increase in EBITDA levels, cash flow from operations (CFO) remained flat at INR1.7 billion in FY19  (FY18:INR1.7 billion) owing to a rise in interest costs, taxes and working capital needs. However, capex incurred to set up a factory at CIDCO-Mumbai led to continued negative free cash flow of INR0.7 billion in FY19 (FY18: negative INR1.3 billion). The net working capital cycle# increased to 20 days in FY19 (FY18: negative three days; FY17: negative 31 days) owing to lower mobilisation advances outstanding. Trade receivables historically included INR1 billion of dues from Telangana Rajiv Swagruha Corporation Limited (TRSCL), out of which INR0.8 billion was received by the company in October 2019.

 

Moreover, for the 12 months ended 31 October 2019, BGSCTPL’s maximum and average utilisation of its fund-based working capital limits stood at 64% and 50% and of its average non-fund-based limits was 76%. The company has an expansionary capex plan of INR1.7 billion in FY20. Ind-Ra expects BGSCTPL to continue to report positive CFO in the future, driven by higher profitability, though the positive impact of the same would be partly offset by higher interest cost, taxes and working capital needs.


Exposure to Group Entities: BGSCTPL extended support to group entities in the form of loans and advances of INR2.9 billion in FY19 (FY18: 2.2 billion) as its operations are yet to pick up. The majority of support was given to Shirke Recreation Enterprise (‘IND BB’/Stable), Teenmurthy Summit Realty LLP, B G Shirke Oil & Gas Pvt. Ltd. and Shirke Club Management LLP; these four entities together accounted for 96% of BGSCTPL’s total loans and advances in FY19 (FY18: 98%). Additionally, in FY19, BGSCTPL provided a corporate guarantee of INR0.3 billion (FY18: INR0.4 billion) to B. G. Shirke Oil & Gas India Private Limited, and a letter of undertaking to the bank for INR0.8 billion (FY18: nil) to Teenmurty Summit Realty LLP.
ratingSensitivities:
Positive: Demonstration of an improvement in the free cash flows (cash flow from operations – interest expenses – capex), resulting in further improvement in credit metrics to sustainable levels, would be positive for the ratings.


Negative: BGSCTPL’s gross coverage (EBITDAR/ interest cost) falling below 3.0x, on a sustained basis, could lead to a negative rating action.
companyProfile:
Incorporated in 1994 (established business in 1944), B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt. Ltd. (BGSCTPL) is the flagship company of the Pune-based Shirke Group. BGSCTPL is primarily engaged in the construction of housing projects for government agencies such as Delhi Development Authority (DDA), Maharashtra Housing and Development Authority (MHADA), and City and Industrial Development Corporation of Maharashtra Ltd (CIDCO).

descriptionAboutIndiaRating:
India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) is India's SEBI registered credit rating agency committed to providing India's credit markets accurate, timely, and prospective credit opinions. Built on a foundation of independent thinking, rigorous analytics, and an open and balanced approach towards credit research, Ind-Ra has grown rapidly during the past decade, gaining significant market presence in India's fixed income market.

Ind-Ra currently maintains coverage of corporate issuers, financial institutions (including banks and insurance companies), finance companies, urban local bodies, and structured finance and project finance companies.

Headquartered in Mumbai, Ind-Ra has seven branch offices located in Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Gurugram, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Pune. Ind-Ra is recognised by the Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India.

Ind-Ra is a 100% owned subsidiary of the Fitch Group.
